page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge is a compute-focused x86_64 server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, it features 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs configured with 2 threads per core. The processor cache architecture includes 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache per core. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. It contains no local disk storage and zero GPU accelerators.

Performance data indicates a distinct functional split between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-threaded benchmarks report lower performance tier placement, including a stress-ng single-core score of 1107.49 and a Geekbench single-core result of 963.0. In contrast, multi-threaded tasks leverage all 32 vCPUs effectively, achieving average benchmark tiers with a multi-core stress-ng score of 23528.93 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8384.0. Uncached memory bandwidth tests record 92.61 GB/sec for reads and 43.13 GB/sec for writes, while PassMark memory testing registers in the lower quartile.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation prioritizes CPU density over large memory footprints. Because no local storage is bundled, storage requirements must be fulfilled via attached network volumes, altering disk performance and cost characteristics. Based on multi-core compute metrics, Redis performance reaching 23.22 million SET operations per second, and static web serving throughput of 13.98 GB/sec, this server type fits multi-threaded backend services, software compilation pipelines, static web hosting, and containerized microservice deployments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge is a compute-focused x86_64 virtual instance built on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 CPU, it provides 16 physical cores, 32 dedicated vCPUs, 33 MB of L3 cache, and 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Network performance is rated at a baseline of 6 Gbps, and no local disk storage or GPUs are included. Performance benchmarks highlight a trade-off between lower single-core execution speeds and capable multi-threaded parallel processing. The instance achieves average results in multi-core tasks, such as software compilation, static web serving at 13.98 GB/sec, and Redis operations at 23.22 million SETs per second. Due to its allocation profile, this server provides cost-efficient multi-threaded compute density suited for batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices requiring moderate memory per thread.
